text:
Travis Konecny scored in overtime in Ottawa on Thursday to finish a 6-5 comeback, the Flyers' first overtime win of the season, days after reports that they could ask him to waive his no-movement clause (RMNB). Jamie Drysdale, who tied it, summed it up: "It was ugly. We didn’t play very well, but we found a way," as PHLY's Charlie O'Connor posted.

Ugly is a fair word for the season. Philadelphia is 8-11-6 and gets 46% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), only 43% at five on five, the kind of share that loses more nights than it wins. The record isn't unlucky either: our points from the play come to 23.2, right around their 22. Rick Tocchet's team is 8% to make the playoffs by our odds.

There are bright spots. Drysdale has 12 points in his last 10 against 5.7 our numbers expected, a hot run worth enjoying but not counting on. Noah Cates, Matvei Michkov and Porter Martone have 62% of the chances together. Trevor Zegras has 2 points in his last 10 against 7.1 expected, which reads more like cold luck than a lost touch.

The questions now are about the future: Konecny's name keeps coming up, and so does Michkov's in trade pitches. What we'd watch is the shot share. Until it climbs, the Flyers are a team selling hope, and maybe veterans.
headline: The Flyers are scrapping while the rumours swirl
